HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Option A: Enter when price hits the lower edge of the black box. Price doesn't hit SL, exit at blue box. R:R approx 1:1.5 Option B: Hold off on entering as in option A and instead see if price makes a deeper retrace. It does, enter at the lower edge of the red box. Price doesn't hit SL, exit at blue box. R:R approx 1:15 Risking 2% on option A you have made 3% Risking 2% on option B you have made 30% Following option B will cause you to miss trades, following option A will cause you to enter every trade. I'm not saying that one is better than the other just that both are possibilities worth being aware of. I wouldn't mind missing a few trades if the ones that I got had R:R's in the double digits. Using 3% risk, you made 5.4%. - point B: your risk to the top of the black box is ~1 grid boxes, or 25 pips and your reward to the lower box is ~13 grid boxes or 325 pips, for a risk:reward of 1:13. Using 3% risk, you made 39%. A is pretty good, B is FAR better. That's why you often see If enter at the utmost extreme with minuscule SL and huge risk:rewards. [ Click to expand ] You need to know the psychological reasons for the drop and rise of the prices after formation of the flag. Rally-base-Drop has a base which is also a flag. When price consolidate in a side ways within a range for a while and breaks one of the sides some times both the sides by faking out then you need to visualize what happened behind the charts. People look left to see where it reacted but forgets to look left of the left. 1] For me there is no specific and only single reason for the formation of important high https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2025-amit-s-journal-and-trading-practice?start=500 8/39 7/27/2018 Amit's Journal and Trading Practice - Page 21 - RTM Community (or low). And the things is that each and every high and low is important according to HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT their respective TFs.Here the TFs means the terms, short term, long term, medium term. You should have eye on the these SDs and should watch and IMAGINE what ITs are trying to do at these levels. Then you can see the decision. Ask yourself who bought, who sold around the highs/lows, SDs etc and who failed how & why. If they failed then where the extreme limit of their failure. It can be a decision point as well as QM if price FO. 2] Targets can be the origin of the move. See the beginning posts of FF RTM thread. 3] Video about CAPs by IF is very good to know about how to draw the boxes. If you are trying to understand PAZ since one year but not understanding then try to change your view to the PAZ. PAZ are the zones where tricks are played and decisions are made (according to my view). You can see gambles journal too as he is doing really good job and now a days active than me. There are sub points of SD. like -Fresh (untested) SD, tested (visited 1 or more time) SD (we call it FTB, 2TB, 3TB...)... -Ignored SD, what happens when SD gets ignored, etc. Take your time to understand the behaviour of price action with supply and demand. Lets say that you expect price to turn somewhere in the black 20/29 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2025-amit-s-journal-and-trading-practice?start=225 7/27/2018 Amit's Journal and Trading Practice - Page 10 - RTM Community box and that once it does you let it run as far as the blue box. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Option A: Enter when price hits the lower edge of the black box. Price doesn't hit SL, exit at blue box. R:R approx 1:1.5 Option B: Hold off on entering as in option A and instead see if price makes a deeper retrace. It does, enter at the lower edge of the red box. Price doesn't hit SL, exit at blue box. R:R approx 1:15 Risking 2% on option A you have made 3% Risking 2% on option B you have made 30% Following option B will cause you to miss trades, following option A will cause you to enter every trade. I'm not saying that one is better than the other just that both are possibilities worth being aware of. I wouldn't mind missing a few trades if the ones that I got had R:R's in the double digits. I don't know what the grid lines represent but let's say they are 25 pips. If you enter at: - point A: your risk to the top of the black box is ~5 grid boxes, or 125 pips and your reward to the lower box is ~9 grid boxes or 225 pips, for a risk:reward of 1:1.8. Using 3% risk, you made 5.4%. - point B: your risk to the top of the black box is ~1 grid boxes, or 25 pips and your reward to the lower box is ~13 grid boxes or 325 pips, for a risk:reward of 1:13. Using 3% risk, you made 39%. A is pretty good, B is FAR better. That's why you often see If enter at the utmost extreme with minuscule SL and huge risk:rewards. QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Amit's Journal and Trading Practice #282 Cleric Offline Trader Posts: 20 Thank you received: 21 milkeyway wrote: https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2025-amit-s-journal-and-trading-practice?start=275 8/30 7/27/2018 Amit's Journal and Trading Practice - Page 12 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Now, this little thing is important, great job making an example, Amit. I should note, that by my observations, this kind of price structure works best when the moves are strong and with LQ. It really fits well into market mechanics. The reason this is a valid setup is because it's a confirmation of sellers' strenght. After initial drop from high, price engulfs previous DP (can be anything. as long as it stands out as a good DP, with strong LQ to and from it) and buyers trying to take control back, but they fail miserably, being smashed by sellers. At this point all those, who were long before or near high, are given opportunity to cover, and they use it, adding fuel to the fire. You need to read the price action story left to right. Price moves from one place to another by consuming orders. If it reacts there then you need to look more back history to know why it reacted there and if not reacted even that you need to look back to know why it didn't reacted. [ Click to expand ] You need to know the psychological reasons for the drop and rise of the prices after formation of the flag. Rally-base-Drop has a base which is also a flag. When price consolidate in a side ways within a range for a while and breaks one of the sides some times both the sides by faking out then you need to visualize what happened behind the charts. People look left to see where it reacted but forgets to look left of the left. 1] For me there is no specific and only single reason for the formation of important high https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2025-amit-s-journal-and-trading-practice?start=500 8/39 7/27/2018 Amit's Journal and Trading Practice - Page 21 - RTM Community (or low). And the things is that each and every high and low is important according to HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT their respective TFs.Here the TFs means the terms, short term, long term, medium term. You should have eye on the these SDs and should watch and IMAGINE what ITs are trying to do at these levels. Then you can see the decision. Ask yourself who bought, who sold around the highs/lows, SDs etc and who failed how & why. If they failed then where the extreme limit of their failure. It can be a decision point as well as QM if price FO. 2] Targets can be the origin of the move. See the beginning posts of FF RTM thread. 3] Video about CAPs by IF is very good to know about how to draw the boxes. If you are trying to understand PAZ since one year but not understanding then try to change your view to the PAZ. PAZ are the zones where tricks are played and decisions are made (according to my view). You can see gambles journal too as he is doing really good job and now a days active than me. But what i did is I learned these concepts separately then then tried to use them together. 1st understand what is supply and demand (SD). SD is not just where price dropped and raised. There are sub points of SD. like -Fresh (untested) SD, tested (visited 1 or more time) SD (we call it FTB, 2TB, 3TB...)... -Ignored SD, what happens when SD gets ignored, etc. Take your time to understand the behaviour of price action with supply and demand. Then pick a 1 topic from marketpedia, lets say FTR. Then start learning and locating FTRs and observe how price behaves at these FTRs. Find the max information about FTR as possible as you can. Ask yourself why FTR occurred. Why price failed to return who failed. etc. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2025-amit-s-journal-and-trading-practice?start=50 9/34 7/27/2018 Amit's Journal and Trading Practice - Page 3 - RTM Community Then slowly slowly learn other topic and while learning them keep posting in home HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT work. Watch videos by IF over and over again and notice what reasons he used to enter trade. Every week watch his all videos and read market pedia again and again and keep finding the concepts on your chart and observe how price behaves. This is a slow process but the more time and hardwork you will give to RTM, there more quickly you can learn. It does take time but you can learn it if you keep fighting with it. Read journals of Dr. Swing and Draft's journal. Very nice explanation is given for the entries. But before that learn the concepts separately one by one. Read trading article discussion thread. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Option A: Enter when price hits the lower edge of the black box. Price doesn't hit SL, exit at blue box. R:R approx 1:1.5 Option B: Hold off on entering as in option A and instead see if price makes a deeper retrace. It does, enter at the lower edge of the red box. Price doesn't hit SL, exit at blue box. R:R approx 1:15 Risking 2% on option A you have made 3% Risking 2% on option B you have made 30% Following option B will cause you to miss trades, following option A will cause you to enter every trade. I'm not saying that one is better than the other just that both are possibilities worth being aware of. I wouldn't mind missing a few trades if the ones that I got had R:R's in the double digits. I don't know what the grid lines represent but let's say they are 25 pips. If you enter at: - point A: your risk to the top of the black box is ~5 grid boxes, or 125 pips and your reward to the lower box is ~9 grid boxes or 225 pips, for a risk:reward of 1:1.8. Using 3% risk, you made 5.4%. - point B: your risk to the top of the black box is ~1 grid boxes, or 25 pips and your reward to the lower box is ~13 grid boxes or 325 pips, for a risk:reward of 1:13. Using 3% risk, you made 39%. A is pretty good, B is FAR better. That's why you often see If enter at the utmost extreme with minuscule SL and huge risk:rewards. Sorry if that's not what was meant or I confused the issue further. As a result we make more, sometimes substantially more from the trade if we are lucky enough to get a deep retrace rather than one that bounces at the periphery of our entry area. But hoping for the deep entry has the drawback of missing entries so I can't say for sure what is best. Sorry if I am not being very clear. To be honest you seem to be doing great so there's no need to think about this kind of stuff until you are ready to go looking for it. So, here, what would you do? You would put your shop at the place where there is too much rush of people. i.e where people can make transactions. Those places can be a Street where many people walk everyday or a marketplace where people go to buy their daily needed products. Same as if you want to catch fish, you have to go to the river. River doesn't come to your home. right ? So, here you found "The places where most of the Transactions happens." The same way, there are specific levels where transactions happens i.e. IT as a Shopkeeper and Retailers are Customers. And those places are where IT can play their tricks because at those levels there is too much rush of retail traders. (People's favorite places / Usual places where they jump into market or out of the market). These levels are like a Marketplace. So, what you need to know (most of you already know) that the places where People like to trade and because of that IT get chance to play tricks with them. So, these places (Market places) are : Support and resistance (horizontal) Support and resistance (Trendline) (I don't use trendline though) Supply and Demand levels Round Numbers (Many times) Important News events Top of the Range Market Bottom of the Range Market Breakout of specific levels. Their stop losses are at nearest high or low. You need to read the price action story left to right. Price moves from one place to another by consuming orders. You need to see how the orders are consumed and what happens when price comes back to that consumption. If it reacts there then you need to look more back history to know why it reacted there and if not reacted even that you need to look back to know why it didn't reacted. Draw horizontal lines on swing high and low and look left for the reason and see if the reason is repeated. Keep in mind about the consumption, decision and PA story. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2025-amit-s-journal-and-trading-practice?start=450 20/37 7/27/2018 Amit's Journal and Trading Practice - Page 19 - RTM Community Consumption and decision is one of the major cause of price movement. [ Click to expand ] You need to know the psychological reasons for the drop and rise of the prices after formation of the flag. Rally-base-Drop has a base which is also a flag. When price consolidate in a side ways within a range for a while and breaks one of the sides some times both the sides by faking out then you need to visualize what happened behind the charts. People look left to see where it reacted but forgets to look left of the left. 1] For me there is no specific and only single reason for the formation of important high https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2025-amit-s-journal-and-trading-practice?start=500 8/39 7/27/2018 Amit's Journal and Trading Practice - Page 21 - RTM Community (or low). And the things is that each and every high and low is important according to HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT their respective TFs.Here the TFs means the terms, short term, long term, medium term. You should have eye on the these SDs and should watch and IMAGINE what ITs are trying to do at these levels. Then you can see the decision. Ask yourself who bought, who sold around the highs/lows, SDs etc and who failed how & why. If they failed then where the extreme limit of their failure. It can be a decision point as well as QM if price FO. 2] Targets can be the origin of the move. See the beginning posts of FF RTM thread. 3] Video about CAPs by IF is very good to know about how to draw the boxes. If you are trying to understand PAZ since one year but not understanding then try to change your view to the PAZ. PAZ are the zones where tricks are played and decisions are made (according to my view). You can see gambles journal too as he is doing really good job and now a days active than me. But what i did is I learned these concepts separately then then tried to use them together. 1st understand what is supply and demand (SD). SD is not just where price dropped and raised. There are sub points of SD. like -Fresh (untested) SD, tested (visited 1 or more time) SD (we call it FTB, 2TB, 3TB...)... -Ignored SD, what happens when SD gets ignored, etc. Take your time to understand the behaviour of price action with supply and demand. Then pick a 1 topic from marketpedia, lets say FTR. Then start learning and locating FTRs and observe how price behaves at these FTRs. Find the max information about FTR as possible as you can. Ask yourself why FTR occurred. Why price failed to return who failed. etc. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2025-amit-s-journal-and-trading-practice?start=50 9/34 7/27/2018 Amit's Journal and Trading Practice - Page 3 - RTM Community Then slowly slowly learn other topic and while learning them keep posting in home HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT work. Watch videos by IF over and over again and notice what reasons he used to enter trade. Every week watch his all videos and read market pedia again and again and keep finding the concepts on your chart and observe how price behaves. This is a slow process but the more time and hardwork you will give to RTM, there more quickly you can learn. It does take time but you can learn it if you keep fighting with it. Read journals of Dr. Swing and Draft's journal. Very nice explanation is given for the entries. But before that learn the concepts separately one by one. Read trading article discussion thread.
